comments.text:
I didn't feel great about our attacking Iran, because if we don't see it thru (which Americans have no stomach for, due to the short-term financial impacts), we leave things worse than they were before. We just bombed the nuclear sites several months ago, and that supposedly was so successful that they would have no chance of nuclear weapons for a very long time. Now the story is very different, and this was the motivation for a full-on attack (Trump has said they likely would have used a nuclear weapon by now, had we not attacked).  They know to bury their gear so far underground (and under granite) to go beyond the capability of our Bunker Busters, so they most likely have all kinds of it still tucked away for when the time is right. We expend massive amounts of money, weapons (have to imagine our stockpiles have been affected greatly, and these weapons take very long periods of time to make, so are we weaker now, for other conflicts that seem to be brewing), and other resources, and the Straits of Hormuz are now apparently only allowing traffic to ships who pay Iran a huge sum of money... But we are saying that's not our problem? We chose to get into this with Israel and no other major players in the military coalition, and initiated the attacks which stirred the hornet's nest up to create this situation, so that is on us.

We hoped the people of Iran would rise up to overthrow the regime there, but this has not happened (which should be fairly predictable, as this formula almost never works). All of this should have been expected and planned for. Unfortunately, if we leave with the same regime (different names/faces don't really seem to matter -- they have the same mentality) in place, and the Straits still controlled by Iran, we leave things worse than we found them and this will most likely create many more future problems for us and many other countries around the world. They seem to be tightly allied with our other enemies (Russia [seems clear that they are getting intelligence from them to do things like blowing up an AWACS, etc.], China, and maybe more), so they can likely build or get more missiles, air defense, and other things as they have in the past, and they can keep making drones (or probably even get them from Russia) to threaten their neighbors. They still have all of their oil and production facilities, so they get keep making bank on that (as well as charging ships to pass thru the Straits) to finance their hostile motivations.

If we leave before the job is done right, how long before we have to do all of this again, or how long before it turns into something bigger and worse? You suggest 3 months but Trump has been suggesting just 2-3 more weeks.  Terrorist regimes seem to be very good at enduring hardship and living back in the Stone Age for a while as we punish them, only to ride it out and get back to business once we have tired of the conflict with them, so giving short timelines to appease the American public also gives the enemy a general estimate of how much longer they need to endure before we go away again. The most sensible person I've heard speak on all of this has been John Bolton - he seems to fully agree that Iran needed to be dealt with, but also that this is not a quick endeavor and leaving prematurely is worse than having never gotten into this in the first place. Like it or not, we are there and in this now, so we have to finish it properly and not just pull the plug because this is creating too much negative press and political fallout.
